prompt: RFC 9114 HTTP/3 SETTINGS values variable-length integer bit sizes
answer:
In RFC 9114, each HTTP/3 SETTINGS identifier and value is encoded as a QUIC variable-length integer.

| Encoding length | Usable value bits | Value range | Prefix in first byte |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 byte | 6 bits | 0–63 | `00` |
| 2 bytes | 14 bits | 0–16,383 | `01` |
| 4 bytes | 30 bits | 0–1,073,741,823 | `10` |
| 8 bytes | 62 bits | 0–4,611,686,018,427,387,903 | `11` |

The two most-significant bits of the first byte indicate the encoding length. Values do not have to use the minimum possible encoding length. RFC 9114’s HTTP/3 Settings registry therefore covers a 62-bit space.
